title: 3 areas under danger heat index — PAGASA
summary: Three areas in the Philippines are under the danger heat index on Tuesday, November 17, the state weather bureau PAGASA said.

blocks.text: Residents in Cainta, Rizal use umbrellas to shield themselves from intense heat yesterday, as the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration reminds the public to stay hydrated and avoid unnecessary outdoor activities.
The Philippine STAR / Miguel de Guzman
MANILA, Philippines — Three areas in the Philippines are under the danger heat index on Tuesday, November 17, the state weather bureau PAGASA said.
In a weather forecast on Tuesday, November 17, the state weather bureau said that the three areas may experience temperatures as high as 42°C.
Heat index readings continue to be recorded by PAGASA due to the effects of the Super El Niño, despite the presence of the northeast monsoon, locally known as amihan.
The following areas may experience a “danger” heat index:
Most parts of the country remain under the extreme caution category, with heat index levels ranging from 33°C to 41°C.
In Metro Manila, the Science Garden in Quezon City is under the same classification, with a forecast heat index of 37°C, while NAIA in Pasay City may experience temperatures of up to 38°C.
